title: Sort and filter controls on Room/Bed views
description: Split out of the original LODGY-39 (too broad as one ticket). Wardens want to filter Room/Bed views to vacant-only or occupied-only, so a full property scan doesn't require mentally filtering a long mixed list. Applies to RoomListScreen, BedGridScreen, and VacantViewScreen (LODGY-21) consistently.
acceptanceCriteria: Room/bed views can filter to vacant-only or occupied-only
Filter state is per-screen and obvious when active (not a silent, easy-to-forget toggle)

history.note: Added following backlog review: splitting LODGY-39, giving LODGY-37/45 a shared PDF prerequisite, and folding in the latest round of direct feedback (a real delete-without-confirmation bug hit on Rooms, a default-language reversal, and new notification/navigation-polish requests).

Starting - adding bed-occupancy aggregate queries (grouped in SQL rather than combining one Flow per room) so RoomListScreen can filter by whether a room still has space, then a status filter on BedGridScreen and on VacantViewScreen. Reusing LODGY-39's FilterChipRow so the three screens read identically.

Filters landed on all three bed-facing screens, sharing one BedFilter (ALL/VACANT/OCCUPIED) and matches() in ui/common/StatusBadge.kt plus the BedFilterChips composable, so the chips look and behave identically wherever they appear. BedGridScreen filters its tiles directly. VacantViewScreen now loads every bed rather than pre-filtering to vacant in the query, and defaults its chip to VACANT - the screen opens exactly as before, but the other two options turn it into a full bed browser; its floor-count and empty-state strings were de-hardcoded from 'vacant' accordingly. RoomListScreen needed a different question, since a room has no status of its own: All / Has space / Full, where 'has space' means at least one vacant bed and 'full' means every bed taken. That needs bed counts per room, so BedDao gained observeOccupancyByFloor (a GROUP BY, not one Flow per room - that would re-emit everything on any bed edit and scale with the property) and each row now shows 'N vacant / M beds'. Filter state is per-screen, always visible as a selected chip, and an empty result says 'Nothing matches this filter' rather than reusing the no-data message. Also added observeOccupancyByHostel in the same pass for LODGY-41. Tests: RoomListViewModelTest covers counts, a bed-less room, and the has-space/full split; VacantViewViewModelTest covers the default and both other filter positions. testDebugUnitTest green.

PASS. AC1: verified on all three screens - RoomListScreen has All / Has space / Full, and BedGridScreen and VacantViewScreen both have All / Vacant / Occupied backed by the shared BedFilter in ui/common/StatusTokens.kt, so the three read the same way. Filtering Room 102's grid to Occupied correctly left only Bed A. VacantViewScreen additionally filters by floor (All floors / Ground / First). AC2: filter state is per-screen and the active chip is visibly selected (filled container vs outlined), so it is obvious when a filter is on.
